notes:
The closing request combines separate evidence scopes. ENGIN-19 records two failed production attempts on October 1 at 13:42:17 and 13:49:53 UTC, with the intended update absent. The quoted acknowledgement covers staging validation from 13:15 to 13:30 UTC. Neither production attempt is covered. Failed publishing does not by itself establish website downtime.

ENGIN-4 concerns an accepted nonproduction recovery exercise. ENGIN-16 concerns another customer's approval issue. Neither proves recovery of Beaconpath's update. September 30 warehouse refreshes differ in attempt counts and must not be summed. The latest September 30 observation shows three successes and no failures. October 1 shows two failures and no successes. Customer/day totals cannot prove release of a particular revision.

The signed renewal PM-2026-0EB803D provides Standard support and incident response. Its correction and termination/refund clauses do not authorize an automatic 10 percent service credit. Hannah's recollection is not contractual permission, and absence of a dated approval in the available records does not prove that no other commercial evidence exists. Ask Finance to review a proposed goodwill credit.

Keep recovery unconfirmed while Ren identifies the intended revision and checks production release evidence and the authorized next step. Hannah can then ask Anika to verify that update. Case labels are not native release IDs. Do not prescribe an unsupported restore, invent revision identifiers, or bypass access restrictions. A concise correction with a limited follow-up is sufficient. The secondary conversations already have answers or acknowledged owners.

example_messages.text:
I'd revise this before closing. ENGIN-19 records two failed production attempts on October 1, at 13:42:17 and 13:49:53 UTC, with the intended update still absent. The acknowledgement covers staging validation from 13:15 to 13:30 UTC. Neither production attempt falls within that scope. This supports blocked publishing, without establishing website downtime.

ENGIN-4 accepted a separate nonproduction recovery exercise. Yesterday's latest report records three successful publishes, while the October 1 report records two failures and no successes. Neither establishes recovery of this update.

The signed renewal PM-2026-0EB803D provides Standard support and incident response. Pages 3–4 contain correction and termination/refund provisions, but no automatic 10% service credit. Hold that promise and ask Finance to review any proposed goodwill credit.

Keep recovery unconfirmed while Ren identifies the intended revision, checks its production release evidence and establishes the authorized next step. Hannah can then ask Anika to verify that exact update. Suggested customer wording: “We're checking the failed launch-page update and will confirm when the intended change is live.”

important_mistakes: Treating the accepted nonproduction exercise as recovery of Beaconpath's production update.
Applying a staging-only, time-bounded acknowledgement to later production attempts.
Claiming website downtime from failed publishing or an absent update.
Summing repeated warehouse refreshes or using September 30 success as proof about October 1.
Promising an automatic percentage credit absent supporting signed terms or a dated approval.
Calling ENGIN-16 a deployed Beaconpath fix, prescribing an unsupported restore or inventing native revision and release IDs.
Responding to secondary conversations despite their explicit answer or acknowledged owner.
reference.reason: An unanswered recent review request proposes premature closure and an unsupported credit promise. A concise correction can separate production impact, internal exercise acceptance and contractual remedies, while leaving the smallest necessary verification open. Equivalent evidence-backed corrections are acceptable without every timestamp or a prescribed recovery method.

scenario: A Customer Success closing note relies on an accepted internal recovery exercise, yesterday's publishing report and an informal commercial recollection. The agent must compare a separate production report, the exact acknowledgement scope, dated warehouse observations and the current signed renewal before recommending closure wording and a limited follow-up.
